## Squachy learns to move

Squachy had eight moods and, for most of the time you were looking at
him, exactly one of them was running: a bob, an arm sway, and a blink on
a perfectly regular timer. This release gives him **eleven new
animations**, rebuilds the wolf costume, and gives the werewolf on the
FIRE background a real howl.

**He squashes and stretches now.** The bob used to move a rigid drawing
up and down, which is the single thing that most reads as a sprite being
translated rather than a character moving. His head sinks into his
shoulders as he lands and extends at the apex, and his shadow spreads as
he gets closer to it. No new shapes — both come off the bob that was
already there.

**His blink is no longer a metronome.** It was one line of arithmetic
that fired both eyes, for the same length, forever. It now picks a
different moment, length and kind inside every window: usually one
ordinary blink, sometimes a double, rarely a long slow one. Regularity
at that scale is most of what makes a face read as a machine rather than
as something alive.

**Speech bubbles grow instead of appearing.** A bubble used to exist on
one frame and not on the frame before it. It now scales up out of
nothing with a small overshoot so it settles rather than snapping to
size.

**A detection makes him double-take.** His head snaps the wrong way
first, holds a beat, then whips back with his shades sliding down his
nose — and **the whole reaction is now scaled by signal strength**. A
weak, distant ping gets a flinch; something sitting on top of you gets a
full stumble backwards, from the same pose maths. You can read proximity
off his body language before you read the log.

**And a pile of things he does on his own:** blowing a bubblegum bubble,
a proper waking stretch and yawn, juggling the last three things he
caught in their own detection colours, holding up binoculars while a
scan runs, and ducking when a flying toaster comes too close — with
something to say about it afterwards. **You can pick him up**: press and
hold him, then drag, and he dangles and kicks until you let go, then
lands in a squash.

**Pacing was 45 seconds of one pose.** His patrol now stops at the far
end of each sweep to sniff the ground, shade his eyes at something
overhead, or scratch behind an ear.

### Two of these were unreachable, not rare

Worth saying plainly, because it was a real bug rather than tuning. The
**packet juggle** was gated on an activity counter that added 30 per
detection against a floor of 50 and bled off at 2 a second — so one
catch never qualified, and two qualified for about five seconds, inside
a window that only gets sampled every twelve to thirty seconds. It could
not fire. The **waking stretch** could only be reached by waking from a
nap, and a nap needs ten full minutes of being ignored before it even
starts. Both are reachable now, and the reasoning is written into the
code so it does not come back.

### SHOW OFF

There is a new **SHOW OFF** row in Settings, under Squachy. It walks him
through every pose he has, back to back, naming each one in his own
speech bubble. Any tap ends it.

It exists because most of what he does is gated behind a random roll, a
real detection, a particular background, or a gesture nobody was ever
told about — so without this there was no way to actually see the set.
The walkthrough now mentions the carry gesture too.

### The wolf costume

The mask was two glowing sockets, a two-pixel jaw bar and five fangs,
and the long fangs came down over his own lenses. It read as teeth
because there was almost nothing else up there to read. It is now a
**skull worn crooked** — a slanted crown, sockets set at different
heights, an angled jaw and a much shorter bite, with the ears 25% longer
and standing clear on top. The tips pass behind the title bar when he
rides high; that is deliberate, and it is what buys the length.

**The pelt on his arms is attached to his arms now.** It used to be four
rectangles at fixed coordinates, which was fine while his arms only ever
hung straight down. They do not: they sway, swing, throw wide on a
startle and go overhead on a stretch, and the pelt stayed exactly where
it was through all of it. It hangs off wherever each arm actually ended
up.

### The werewolf finally howls

Ten taps on the moon on the FIRE background still summons him, but he no
longer just stands there. **"Don't Be a SKID!" now lands and clears
before he moves** — it used to be on screen right through the howl, so
his one spoken beat and his one physical beat happened at the same time
and neither of them read.

Then he coils, snaps up, throws his head back three times as far as
before, flings both arms wide, and lets out an **AWOOOO** with an echo
rolling off behind it and three rings of sound leaving his muzzle. The
fire he is standing behind surges as he hits the note and settles as it
dies.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: eleven new Squachy animations, including squash-and-stretch, irregular blinking, bubble pop-in and a signal-strength-scaled detection recoil
- **Added**: press and hold Squachy then drag to carry him around
- **Added**: SHOW OFF row in Settings — every pose, back to back, each one named
- **Added**: three new beats during his patrol, so pacing is not one pose for 45 seconds
- **Changed**: the wolf mask is a crooked skull with a much shorter bite and 25% longer ears
- **Fixed**: the wolf pelt follows his arms instead of hanging in mid-air
- **Fixed**: the packet juggle and the waking stretch were unreachable, not rare
- **Changed**: the werewolf coils, rears, howls with an echo, and drives the fire while he does it
- **Changed**: toaster ducking is once every 30 seconds instead of near-constant
- **Note**: the wolf ear tips pass behind the title bar at the top of a bounce — that clearance is what makes them full length
